en: Heating an aerosol spray can increases the gas pressure inside, which can cause the metal container to explode dangerously.
Boiling tap water for at least one minute causes a physical change that kills harmful bacteria before you drink it.
When iron nails react with oxygen and water to form rust, a chemical change occurs that can cause tetanus infections.
Pouring water on burning cooking oil is dangerous because water is denser than oil and will instantly vaporize, spreading the fire.
You must shake liquid antibiotic suspensions before use because the solid medicine particles settle at the bottom of the liquid mixture.
Milk turning sour is a chemical change where bacteria produce lactic acid, making the spoiled drink unsafe for your health.
Sweat cooling your skin is a physical change where liquid water absorbs heat from your body to become a gas.
Cooking pots have plastic or wooden handles because these materials are poor thermal conductors that protect your hands from burns.
Inhaling smoke from burning plastic releases toxic chemical mixtures into your lungs, which can cause severe respiratory health problems.
Chewing rice mixes it with saliva, starting a chemical change that breaks down starches into simpler sugars for energy.
Gasoline evaporates quickly into a highly flammable gas at room temperature, making its vapors dangerous to ignite near open flames.
Life jackets keep you afloat in water because their lightweight foam materials are less dense than the surrounding liquid water.
